rulings.reason: The instruction is a pure presence-detector for forum/repost/upvote references, so a 10 records that the joke is about the venue rather than that it lands. Nothing in the text asks whether the meta-reference is executed wittily, so the score is a topic/venue fingerprint with no attached quality claim.

Rating how standardised and pre-circulated the wording feels measures the item's provenance -- how long it has been in circulation before this posting -- and the text explicitly disclaims scoring cleverness. Marked mixed because a joke survives decades of reprinting partly because the construction is genuinely good, so the same upstream cause also carries real quality.

The dominant axis is how widely held the presupposed knowledge is, which would zero a tightly built joke merely for using specialist or regional vocabulary -- that is a fact about audience composition, not about the joke. Marked mixed because the second half of the composite, instant resolution on the punchline, plausibly does track genuine construction quality.

The instruction scores the amount of orthographic or phonetic distortion demanded and explicitly says to ignore the ingenuity of the result, making it a pun-type descriptor rather than a quality judgment. Marked mixed because for pun-based jokes the effortful re-spelling or re-saying can itself be the mechanism that produces the laugh.
